[stop_reason: hop_cap_reached | hops used: 4/4] Analyst summary: **Investigation summary – “BP disruption reported 20‑Apr‑2010 (Deepwater Horizon)”** | Tier | Company (down‑stream or alternative supplier) | Why it appears in the supply graph | Evidence gathered | |------|-----------------------------------------------|------------------------------------|-------------------| | **Tier 1** | **Indian Oil (India – Oil & Gas Producer)** | Listed as a downstream consumer of refined fuels and lubricants supplied by BP. | • No company‑specific filing was retrieved (no `get_supplier_info` call left).
• The only mention of the 20‑Apr‑2010 event is in BP’s own filing (see result 1 below). No direct reference to Indian Oil. | | | **Volkswagen (Germany – Automotive)** | Receives fuel, lubricants and possibly petrochemical feedstocks from BP; flagged by the graph as a downstream customer. | • `get_supplier_info` for Volkswagen returned *no filings on record*.
• A corpus search for “BP Deepwater Horizon impact … Volkswagen” returned only generic BP event records (see result 1) and no VW‑specific comment. | | | **Ford Motor (USA – Automotive)** | Uses BP fuel/lubricants; appears in Tier 2 but is a major downstream OEM. | • No Ford filing mentioning the BP incident was found (the only Ford record returned (result 10) discusses internal product‑development plans, not the spill). | | | **General Motors (USA – Automotive)** *[present in the raw graph list under “general motors”]* | Same rationale as Ford/Volkswagen. | • No GM filing or corpus mention linking it to the BP event was retrieved. | | | **POSCO (South Korea – Steel)** | Uses BP‑derived crude and fuel for steel‑making processes; flagged by the graph. | • No POSCO filing was examined (no tool calls remaining).
• No corpus hit tying POSCO to the Deepwater Horizon incident. | | | **ZF TRW Automotive (USA – Auto components)** | Supplies safety‑system parts to OEMs that in turn buy BP fuel/lubricants; appears in Tier 2. | • Two corpus records (results 2 and 4/5) give ZF TRW’s sales breakdown by OEM (Volkswagen, Ford, GM). These confirm the company’s downstream exposure but do **not** mention any impact from the BP spill. | | | **BorgWarner (USA – Auto‑drivetrain)** | Supplies power‑train components to OEMs that are fuel consumers; appears in Tier 2. | • Two corpus records (results 8 and 9) show BorgWarner’s sales percentages to Volkswagen and Ford, confirming its reliance on the same downstream market but again without any reference to the BP event. | | | **Other Tier‑1/Tier‑2 firms** (e.g., *Jordan Petroleum Refinery, CPC Corp/Taiwan, Grupo Pochteca, LG Chem, Formosa Petrochemical, etc.) | All are listed as downstream users of BP’s refined fuels, petrochemicals or lubricants. | • No individual filings were retrieved for any of these companies (tool budget exhausted).
• No corpus hits directly linking them to the 20‑Apr‑2010 incident were returned. | ### Core evidence about the disruption itself | Source | Date / Event | Key excerpt | |--------|--------------|-------------| | **BP filing – “trigger_24_bp_2010”** (search result 1) | 20‑Apr‑2010 | *“Blowout and explosion on the Deepwater Horizon rig killed 11 workers and caused the largest marine oil spill in history, triggering a US deep‑water drilling moratorium.”* | | **BP filing – “trigger_24_bp_2010”** (same record) | 20‑Apr‑2010 | *Category: Industrial accident; Location: Gulf of Mexico, USA.* | These two excerpts are the only direct documentary confirmations that a major incident at BP occurred on the requested date. ### What could **not** be confirmed * No company‑specific SEC filing (Volkswagen, Ford, GM, POSCO, Indian Oil, etc.) mentions the Deepwater Horizon event or any supply‑chain impact arising from it. * No public statement was found linking the listed downstream customers to a material disruption of fuel, lubricant or petrochemical supplies caused by the spill. * For many Tier 1/Tier 2 firms (e.g., Jordan Petroleum Refinery, CPC Corp/Taiwan, LG Chem, Formosa Petrochemical, etc.) we have only the structural connection from the supply‑graph; no additional filings or corpus mentions were retrieved to verify actual exposure. ### Overall assessment - **Structurally at risk:** The traversal shows a very large network (≈150 companies) that could be affected by a disruption at BP, spanning automotive OEMs (Volkswagen, Ford, GM), auto‑components suppliers (ZF TRW, BorgWarner), steel producers (POSCO, ArcelorMittal, etc.), chemicals and petrochemicals firms, and regional fuel distributors (Indian Oil, Jordan Petroleum Refinery). - **Evidence of impact:** The only concrete evidence we have is BP’s own filing confirming the Deepwater Horizon blow‑out on 20 Apr 2010. No downstream company in our limited data set explicitly documents a supply interruption, loss of product, or financial effect tied to that event. - **Confidence level:** Because the investigation was constrained to four tool calls, we could verify only BP’s own announcement and a handful of generic sales‑to‑OEM disclosures for two component suppliers. The lack of direct statements from downstream firms means we cannot confirm *actual* operational or financial disruption beyond the structural risk indicated by the graph. **Conclusion:** The supply‑graph indicates that many major automotive, steel, chemicals and fuel‑distribution companies are **potentially exposed** to a BP disruption in April 2010. The only documented fact is the Deepwater Horizon accident itself (BP filing). No downstream company filings or corpus mentions were found that explicitly confirm material impacts on those firms. Consequently, while structural risk is high, concrete evidence of realized disruption for the listed companies remains **unverified** within the limits of this investigation.
